W1 (mechanism), after E026.

**Tip: E026**
- E023 math with a 20 px phase added at the start: 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of 225 steps (9.0 true epochs, batch 2000).
- Muon on the conv filters. Filters are renormalized every step, there is no filter wd, and Newton-Schulz runs 3 steps.
- SGD with wd 0.006 on the BN biases, whitening bias and head. Lookahead exponent 3. CUDA graphs.
- Score: 6.017 s, 0.7540. The true mean is probably about 0.7535, so the margin over 0.753 is close to zero.
- Correction: every idea runs on the current tip. My E024–E026 time misses came from forecasting on E017 timings.

**Noise**
- Rebuilding the same commit: about ±0.04 pp.
- Any change to RNG use or step count reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.3 pp (E016 vs its held-out seeds: +0.43).
- At 3 seeds, any effect under 0.3 pp is unreadable.

**Time model (GPU-bound, follows pixel-steps)**
- Train time is about steps × pixel fraction × about 27 ms per 32 px step, plus about 0.25 s of fixed cost.
- E026: replacing 15% of steps at 24 px with 20 px gave −2.9%. E024: 28→26 px gave −2%. E023: −0.5 epoch gave −5.3%.
- Width cuts return about 50% of their MAC savings (E021). Small maps are less efficient, so their per-pixel cost is higher.
- FLOP estimate: about 0.9 GFLOP forward per 32 px image, about 5.4 TFLOP per 32 px step. That implies a high achieved rate (about 100+ TFLOP/s), so kernel levers are small.
- Per-step overhead (Muon on small matrices, Lookahead) is a few percent, so a larger batch saves little time and mostly cuts steps.
- The whitening bias keeps requires_grad after its LR goes to 0, so the backward pass always runs through group 1. FreezeOut-style detaching would remove real work (about 15% of a 32 px step).

**Accuracy exchange rates (pp per 10% of time)**
- Epochs: about 0.25–0.3.
- Width: about 0.3–0.45.
- Resolution depends on the phase. Early phases (low LR warm-up, under 15% of steps) are cheap: E026 cost about 0. Middle and late phases are expensive (E011, E018, E024: about 1 pp or more per 10%).
- Mechanism: features learned early are coarse and get overwritten. The 28 and 32 px phases near and after the LR peak set the final representation, and so does the BN/EMA calibration.

**Measured mechanisms**
- Lookahead/EMA: +1 pp. Muon plus batch 2000: +0.5 pp (confounded). Resizing: −20% time for about −0.5 pp.
- Flat within noise: label smoothing, Muon lr ×1.5, LR floor, wd ×0.5 / ×0.25, alpha exponent 2 (discarded).
- The regime is insensitive to optimizer and regularization knobs. No 0.3 pp booster exists among the scalar knobs.

**Strategy**
- The margin is about 0. Every time cut must pay for itself in accuracy.
- Options: a micro-trim of epochs, more early low-res work (for example, extend 20 px to about 25% of steps), or backward truncation.
- Selection and larger batch most likely act like step cuts, at an equal or worse exchange rate than the epoch dial.

**Unsure**
- Held-out mean of E026.
- Whether the 20 px share can grow further.
- Per-layer efficiency.
- PCIe transfer to the judge: the 40-seed bar of 0.75 has more slack than 0.753.

I038 discarded so branch (b) 219 steps: -2.7% time, ~-0.07pp expected but RNG reshuffle ±0.3 on a zero margin
Saves ~15% of the last 25% of steps (~0.25 s, about 4%), but annealing group-1 LR early and freezing it cost about 0.2-0.4 pp
Acts like a ~9% step cut. Dropping easy samples under LS 0.3 gains little, so the exchange rate is about the same as or worse than the epoch dial
20% fewer steps (and Lookahead updates) at a short horizon cost about 0.3-0.5 pp, and per-step overhead is small, so the time win is only about 3%
Renormalized filters plus orthogonalized updates make the lr an effective-rotation knob that is flat near 0.24-0.36. Doubling it is more likely to hurt slightly than to add 0.2 pp

cruxes: What is the held-out seeds 3–12 mean of E026? If it is at or above 0.755, there is room for epoch or early low-res trims; if it is around 0.753, every trim fails.
Can the 20 px warm-up phase grow (for example to 25–30% of steps, or start at 16 px) at no accuracy cost? That would show early-phase resolution is a free lever, unlike the middle and late phases.
Does the backward pass through group 1 really cost about 15% of a 32 px step (profiler, I040)? This sets whether FreezeOut is worth its accuracy risk.
